[Section] Related Work
[source_id=20] Pretrained embeddings have pushed baselines on a variety of question answering datasets BIBREF8, BIBREF9. Generally, the pretrained models are fine-tuned to the specific task BIBREF10, BIBREF3 but recent work has applied the models without the fine-tuning step BIBREF11, BIBREF0.
[source_id=21] There is a wide range of literature analyzing linguistic knowledge stored in pretrained embeddings BIBREF12, BIBREF13, BIBREF14, BIBREF15, BIBREF16, BIBREF17, BIBREF18, BIBREF19.
[source_id=22] Concerning negation the following papers are of interest: BIBREF20 analyze the grammatical knowledge captured by BERT. In a case study, they test for correct licensing environments for negative polarity items. They study a set of classifiers distinguishing between grammatically correct and incorrect sentences. We take a different approach by focusing on factual knowledge stored in negated statements. Grammatically correct statements can still be factually false (e.g., “General relativity, Newton develop”).
[source_id=23] BIBREF21 investigate the understanding of function words – among them negation particles – using an entailment- and classification-based approach. They analyze the ability of different model architectures and training objectives to capture knowledge of single sentences. The models are fine-tuned to the task of interest. We on the other hand question to what extend factual knowledge present in negated statements is indirectly acquired during pretraining.
[source_id=24] BIBREF22 defines three psycholinguistic diagnostics for language models and applies them in a case study to BERT. Negation is examined using a dataset of 72 simple sentences querying for category membership. A supplementary dataset of 16 sentences queries again for the "to be" relation only but including more natural sentence structure. Our work covers 51,329 negated statements covering a wide range of topics and relations. In the SQuAD based dataset we cover more natural language in terms of context and relation. In contrast to BIBREF22, we do not see a reliable preference of the true completions to false in the more natural negated statements.
[source_id=25] BIBREF23 test for comprehension of minimally modified statements in an adversarial setup while trying to keep the overall semantics the same. We try to maximize the change in semantics and invert meaning.
